bull.b: Sustained double‑digit top‑line growth alongside high gross and operating margins indicates a scalable, high‑margin licensing model. Durable margins create room to invest in product, rights acquisition, and platform features, supporting cash generation and competitive positioning over months.

Rapid growth in custom and AI‑related offerings, reinforced by a multi‑year OpenAI display partnership, shifts the firm toward higher‑value, differentiated services. This diversifies revenue sources, improves monetization of licensed assets, and embeds Getty in emerging AI distribution channels long term.

bull.t: High recurring revenue and strong retention
bull.b: A majority of revenue from subscriptions with very high retention rates provides predictable, recurring cash flows. Stable subscription mix supports long‑term LTV economics, smoother revenue visibility, and a foundation to upsell higher‑margin custom and enterprise offerings over multiple quarters.

bear.t: Elevated leverage and large debt load
bear.b: Very high leverage constrains financial flexibility, raises interest obligations and refinancing risk, and limits ability to fund strategic investments. With sizable upcoming interest (~$194M est.) and debt maturities, leverage remains a material multi‑month structural vulnerability.

bear.t: Net losses and negative shareholder returns
bear.b: Despite solid operating margins, persistent net losses and negative ROE signal earnings volatility after financing and one‑offs. Continued bottom‑line deficits weaken equity accumulation and limit capacity for buybacks/dividends, making recovery dependent on sustained margin and cash‑flow improvement.

Walking away from the merger removes potential scale and cost synergies and triggers a special note redemption, forcing balance‑sheet adjustments. The required redemption and active financing review create structural uncertainty around funding, leverage and creditor claims for months ahead.
